findings.title: smart-search-router (PreToolUse:Grep, registered-active) feeds the model's raw Grep `pattern` into an execSync cmd.exe shell-string (`rg "${escaped}"`), escaping only " and $ — the cmd.exe danger set (& | > < ^ %VAR%) passes through. Fires on EVERY Grep whenever the TLDR daemon is down. D5a saw this site and punted it as 'minor'.
causal_links: extends D5a triage (D5a labeled smart-search-router.ts:101 'minor, bounded by timeout+2>/dev/null' — re-rated here as live S1 injection on the Grep hot path)
findings.telemetry: Stop the TLDR daemon (or run where it never started), issue a Grep whose pattern contains a cmd.exe metachar — e.g. pattern `foo & calc` or `x>poc.txt` — and observe the side-effect (file written / second command run). Count: on Windows `execSync` with no `shell` option uses %ComSpec% = cmd.exe; the escape regex at line 100 only handles " and $. Also note `2>/dev/null` at line 102 is a no-op on cmd.exe (creates a literal file named 'null').
findings.observe_how: main() at line 447 reads `pattern = input.tool_input.pattern` (the model's Grep regex) and at line 455 calls extractTarget(pattern) UNCONDITIONALLY before any literal/early-return. extractTarget -> lookupSymbol(pattern) -> tldrSearch(`def ${pattern}`) / `class ${pattern}` / `${pattern} =`. tldrSearch tries the daemon first but falls through to ripgrepFallback(pattern) when the daemon is indexing/unavailable OR on ANY thrown error (catch, lines 89-92). ripgrepFallback builds `rg "${escaped}" "${projectDir}" --type py ... 2>/dev/null` with escaped = pattern.replace(/"/g,'\\"').replace(/\$/g,'\\$') and runs it through execSync (cmd.exe). cmd.exe treats & | > < ^ and %VAR% as live metacharacters — none are escaped — so a Grep pattern containing them executes/redirects. Same remediation class as D5a-01/02/03: drop the shell-string, use spawnSync('rg', [escaped, projectDir, '--type','py',...], {shell:false}).

findings.title: daemon-client Windows TCP path double-shells the same model-controlled Grep pattern: query JSON (containing `pattern`) is interpolated into a PowerShell command, which is then wrapped in an execSync cmd.exe string (`powershell -Command "..."`). Inner PS escape covers ' only; outer cmd.exe escape covers " only — % & ^ < > | reach cmd.exe live.
causal_links: same model-controlled pattern as GAP4-01 (smart-search-router queryDaemonSync({cmd:'search',pattern}))
D5a flagged daemon-client.ts:582/589 as 'connInfo.path/psCommand, not user content' — that triage missed that `input` = JSON.stringify(query) carries the model's search `pattern`
findings.telemetry: On Windows with the TLDR daemon reachable over TCP (connInfo.type==='tcp'), issue a Grep whose pattern contains a cmd.exe metachar (% ^ & < > |) and check for an injected effect through the outer `powershell -Command "..."` cmd.exe wrapper. The inner PS layer escapes ' -> '' (correct for PS), but the outer execSync only does psCommand.replace(/"/g,'\\"'); cmd.exe metachars in the pattern are untouched at the outer layer.
findings.observe_how: smart-search-router.ts:76 calls queryDaemonSync({ cmd: 'search', pattern }, projectDir) with the model's Grep pattern. In daemon-client.ts queryDaemonSync (line 544) sets input = JSON.stringify(query) (line 565) — the pattern is now inside `input`. On the Windows branch (connInfo.type==='tcp'), input is interpolated into psCommand via `$writer.WriteLine('${input.replace(/'/g, "''")}')` (line 575), and the whole psCommand is run via execSync(`powershell -Command "${psCommand.replace(/"/g,'\\"')}"`) (line 582). Two shells, two escape regexes, neither covering the cmd.exe metacharacter set the OUTER layer is exposed to. A pattern containing %FOO% / & / ^ / > is interpreted by the outer cmd.exe. Remediation: pass the daemon payload over a real socket (net.Socket) or via spawnSync('powershell', ['-Command', psScript], {shell:false}) so no cmd.exe wrap and no string interpolation of `input` into a -Command argument.

The cross-cutting injection-surface enumeration (scripts/*.mjs, MCP tool-arg interpolation, and non-memory shell sinks like the Grep router) was never swept until this gap-fill — and it surfaced two live S1 sinks D5a had explicitly down-rated to 'lower-risk'.

Grep hot-path shell sink (NEW S1, was D5a 'minor'): smart-search-router.ts (PreToolUse:Grep, REGISTERED ACTIVE in settings.json) — model's tool_input.pattern -> extractTarget (unconditional, line 455) -> lookupSymbol -> tldrSearch(`def ${pattern}`) -> ripgrepFallback -> execSync(`rg "${escaped}"...`) on cmd.exe, escaping only "/$ (omits & | > < ^ %VAR%), fallback fires whenever daemon down or on any throw -> GAP4-01.

DB-returned content is run through sanitizeMemoryContent (line 690, WS-0.2 prompt-injection defense). Correctly hardened; folded into GAP4-03 as the contrast that shows the store-side D5a sinks are not systemic.

notes:
Read-only review at working tree (review SHA 86b8f60). No edits, no test execution, no state changes. All evidence read directly from live source (smart-search-router.ts, daemon-client.ts, memory-awareness.ts, the 10 scripts/*.mjs) and the two on-disk review artifacts D5a.json / WF1-STATE.json (cited as scope evidence, not as findings — they live under docs/reviews/ which is review-context, not a finding target).

HEADLINE: D5b is a genuine gap. D5a was correctly scoped to the memory store/recall hot path and named the 3 real S0/S1 store-side sinks, but its manifest explicitly down-rated two OTHER model-controlled shell sinks — the Grep router's ripgrep fallback and the Windows daemon PowerShell path — to 'minor' / 'not user content'. Both are wrong on the Windows shell this repo actually runs (execSync -> cmd.exe per the repo's own windows-platform.md), and both carry the SAME model-controlled value (the Grep tool_input.pattern) into a shell with escaping that omits the cmd.exe danger set (& | > < ^ %VAR%). GAP4-01 fires on every Grep when the TLDR daemon is down; GAP4-02 is the daemon-reachable Windows path. These are the WF-1 'exploitable-injection' S1 class the D5b dimension was meant to enumerate.

CLEARED (the other half of D5b's value): the scripts/*.mjs shell:true sites are all clean (static/harness-generated args, no untrusted free-text), the supply-chain update-blocklist gh-api url is constant-built, and the MCP tool-arg surface has no new shell sink. The memory-awareness RECALL path is a positive — array-arg spawn + DB-content sanitization — confirming the store-side D5a sinks are a specific-call-site bug class, not a systemic one. Recommendation: keep D5b in the re-run scope (do NOT treat as covered by D5a); fix GAP4-01/02 with the same spawnSync-array remediation D5a prescribes for the store-side trio, since all five share one root pattern: untrusted/model text interpolated into an execSync shell-string instead of passed as spawnSync array args.
